children: Revenue surges 78 per cent to Rs 24,138 crore as Blinkit drives quick-commerce growth; company announces restructuring of its going-out business and changes to its investment in Adonmo

Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a 92.3 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 125 crore for the second quarter of FY27, but the result fell short of market estimates of Rs 304 crore. Revenue rose 77.6 per cent to Rs 24,138 crore in the quarter ended September 2026, from Rs 13,590 crore a year earlier.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased to Rs 752 crore from Rs 239 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, Ebitda also missed the estimate of Rs 776 crore, while the margin came in at 3.1 per cent, against expectations of 3.3 per cent.

The results highlight strong growth across Eternal’s businesses, particularly quick commerce, even as rising operating costs continue to weigh on profitability. Total revenue exceeded the estimate of Rs 23,447 crore.

Eternal’s quick-commerce business, Blinkit, remained a key growth driver during the quarter. The segment’s net order value rose 79.3 per cent year-on-year to Rs 20,940 crore, while the company continued expanding its store network.

Blinkit added 308 stores, taking its total to 2,751. Eternal has set a target of more than 3,500 stores by March 2027 and 5,000 by March 2028, reflecting its continued investment in the fast-growing quick-commerce market.

The expansion comes amid intense competition in India’s instant-delivery sector, where companies are investing in new outlets, logistics and delivery infrastructure to capture a larger share of consumer spending.

Eternal’s food-delivery business, operated through Zomato, also recorded growth. Its net order value increased 21.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 11,445 crore, while adjusted Ebitda rose 25 per cent to Rs 627 crore.

The performance points to continued momentum in the core food-delivery business alongside the faster expansion of Blinkit. However, the company’s consolidated profitability remained below analyst expectations.
Alongside its quarterly results, Eternal announced plans to consolidate its Going-out India business under its wholly owned subsidiary, Zomato Entertainment (ZEPL).

The company plans to transfer the business to ZEPL through a slump sale for Rs 130.76 crore. It also intends to consolidate similar operations currently run by subsidiaries Orbgen Technologies and Wasteland Entertainment under the same entity. The restructuring is aimed at streamlining the group’s going-out operations.

Eternal also plans to restructure its investment in advertising technology company Adonmo through a share swap involving Mygate, the community-management platform operated by Vivish Technologies. Under the proposed transaction, Eternal will acquire a 5.4 per cent stake in Mygate for approximately Rs 156 crore by transferring its investment in Adonmo. The transaction is expected to be completed by December 5, 2026.

Eternal’s total expenses rose 75 per cent year-on-year to Rs 24,166 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 13,813 crore a year earlier. The increase reflects the costs associated with scaling its businesses, including quick-commerce expansion.

The company’s results underline the contrast between rapid revenue growth and the challenge of translating that growth into earnings. While profit nearly doubled from a relatively low base, the miss against estimates suggests that operating costs and investment requirements remain important factors for investors to monitor.
